title: Phase A: Wake & reconnect - eliminate zombie-socket reconnect stall
description:
# Phase A: Wake & reconnect — eliminate the zombie-socket reconnect stall

## Problem
Recovery is *decided* (`reconcileWake` -> `ATTEMPT_RECONNECT` -> `RECONNECTING` -> `connectWebSocket`) but not *executed* after OS resume, because `connectWebSocket()` refuses to replace a half-open socket. We also lack proactive wake detection and robust alarm re-arming.

## Evidence
- `src/background/index.ts:734-768` — `connectWebSocket()` early-returns when `isConnected()` (readyState OPEN) is true; the dispose/recreate block sits *below* the return and is unreachable for a half-open socket.
- `src/app/ws/client.ts:64-68` — `isConnected()` checks only `readyState === OPEN`; `:363-368` — `isConnectionHealthy()` requires a server `nop` within 60s (`lastNopAt` is stale after sleep).
- `manifest.json:19-25` — no `idle` permission; no `chrome.idle` usage anywhere in src.
- `src/app/session/index.ts:519` — `websocketHealthCheck` (1-min) alarm created only during full network init; `src/background/index.ts:1719-1730` re-arms only `longSleepRecovery` at startup.

## Children
- A1 dispose stale sockets (core fix — land first).
- A2 chrome.idle wake trigger.
- A3 re-arm recovery alarms idempotently.
- A4 nop-timeout watchdog (depends on A1).
- A5 keepalive interval correctness (minor).

## Success criteria
All Phase A children closed; a `READY`/`RECONNECTING` state with a half-open or null socket reliably rebuilds the socket; recovery no longer depends on a full network init having run during the current service-worker generation.
acceptance_criteria: All Phase A children closed; half-open/null socket reliably rebuilt on wake without manual Force Wake.

title: Post-sleep wake reliability & SMS delivery/visibility
description:
# Post-sleep wake reliability & SMS delivery/visibility

## Purpose
Fix two recurring, partly-coupled defects in this Manifest V3 Pushbullet client:
1. After extended computer sleep/hibernate, the extension can fail to reconnect its WebSocket and gets stuck (icon stays "connecting"/yellow), so no pushes or SMS arrive until a manual Force Wake.
2. Incoming SMS frequently never displays — neither as a desktop notification nor in the popup list.

These are coupled: Pushbullet delivers SMS/MMS only as **transient real-time ephemerals** over the WebSocket and never replays them. A dead socket (defect 1) therefore permanently loses SMS (defect 2).

## Continuity (do not re-file prior work)
- Builds on the CLOSED epic `pushbullet-chrome-extension-audit-p1-wake`, which fixed the state-machine decision (a stale persisted `READY` no longer blocks reconnect) and introduced `reconcileWake()`. This epic fixes the **residual execution gaps** that survived that work.
- `isValidPush()` already admits `sms_changed` (closed `pushbullet-chrome-extension-rrg.2.1`).

## Phases
- Phase A — Wake & reconnect: make the *already-decided* reconnect actually run (dispose zombie/half-open sockets), add proactive wake detection, re-arm recovery alarms, and self-heal dead sockets.
- Phase B — SMS: stop wiping received SMS from the cache, surface encrypted SMS, fetch SMS thread history, and add diagnostics.

## Global success criteria
- After OS resume from a >1h sleep, the extension re-establishes the WebSocket within one alarm/idle cycle with NO manual Force Wake.
- A text received while connected reliably produces a desktop notification AND remains visible in the popup across refreshes and service-worker restarts.
- Encrypted SMS with no configured password produces a clear, actionable prompt rather than silence.
- New tests encode the post-hibernate half-open socket and the SMS-persistence cases.

## Out of scope
- Reply-to-SMS / full conversation compose UX beyond showing recent threads (future epic).
- Server-side Pushbullet/phone configuration (the user must enable SMS sync on the phone; if E2EE is on, the same password must be set in Options).
acceptance_criteria: After OS resume the WebSocket reliably reconnects; incoming SMS reliably notifies and persists across refresh/restart; new tests cover half-open socket and SMS persistence.

title: Files: lock down notification-data and reconnect message contracts
description:
## File Scope
Primary files:
- `src/background/index.ts`
- `src/lib/security/message-validation.ts`
- `src/types/domain.ts`
- `src/notification-detail/index.ts`

Related UI senders/tests:
- `src/popup/index.ts`
- `src/options/index.ts`
- `tests/lib/message-validation.test.ts`
- `tests/notification-detail/notification-detail.test.ts`

## Verified Problem
`src/background/index.ts` handles notification detail retrieval through two paths:

```ts
if (message.type === "GET_PUSH_DATA") { ... }
else if (message.action === MessageAction.GET_NOTIFICATION_DATA) { ... }
```

The privileged guard validates `message.action`. A `GET_PUSH_DATA` request sent via `message.type` bypasses the privileged action set. `MessageAction.GET_NOTIFICATION_DATA` is also absent from `PRIVILEGED_ACTIONS`. The manual reconnect action is a string literal in popup/options/background and in the privileged set.

## Required Work
- Move `GET_PUSH_DATA` onto the action contract or remove it in favor of `GET_NOTIFICATION_DATA`.
- Add the notification-data action to privileged validation.
- Add `ATTEMPT_RECONNECT = 'attemptReconnect'` to `MessageAction` and replace string literals.
- Keep response shapes stable for notification detail, popup, and options pages.
- Add tests for invalid external senders and valid extension-page senders.

## Exclusions
Do not refactor unrelated background message branches. Do not change notification payload storage semantics beyond sender validation.
acceptance_criteria: GET_PUSH_DATA and GET_NOTIFICATION_DATA require trusted extension senders; GET_PUSH_DATA uses MessageAction/action dispatch instead of message.type; attemptReconnect is represented by MessageAction; notification-detail, popup, options, validation, and background handlers use the same enum contract; tests prove external senders are rejected and internal pages still work.
notes: Implemented MessageAction.GET_PUSH_DATA action dispatch, added MessageAction.ATTEMPT_RECONNECT, privileged validation for GET_PUSH_DATA/GET_NOTIFICATION_DATA/ATTEMPT_RECONNECT, and tests for external rejection plus extension-page success. Verified with focused message/notification tests, popup/options tests, typecheck, and lint.

title: Comprehensive audit remediation program
description:
## Purpose
This epic merges the hibernate-resume bead `pushbullet-chrome-extension-i1g` with the full audit findings. The common theme is operational truth: the extension currently lets persisted state, in-memory globals, alarm callbacks, WebSocket callbacks, popup messages, and debug tooling each carry partial truth.

## Audit Evidence
The audit found five problem families:

```text
1. Lifecycle truth is split between persisted READY, in-memory globals, alarms, and socket state.
2. Sensitive payloads are logged, persisted, exported, and rendered by debug tooling.
3. Incremental cursors advance before push processing is durable or replay-safe.
4. Popup/options/background message contracts and API ownership have drifted.
5. Tests and lint gates are too weak for the lifecycle and security surface.
```

The hibernate bug is the first visible failure. The same root architecture also affects popup wake, health-check wake, manual reconnect, startup, debug export, and incremental processing.

## Target Hierarchy
```text
Comprehensive audit remediation program
├── Phase 1: wake/reconnect correctness
│   ├── existing bead: pushbullet-chrome-extension-i1g
│   ├── ensureConfigLoaded no-op repair
│   ├── WebSocket permanent error routing
│   └── READY state semantic repair
├── Phase 2: privacy and render safety
├── Phase 3: cursor and processing durability
├── Phase 4: message/API/lifecycle architecture
└── Phase 5: tests, lint, and coverage gates
```

- Debug dashboard dynamic data cannot become executable markup.

title: Phase B: SMS delivery & display
description:
# Phase B: SMS delivery & display

## Problem
The SMS notification code works in the happy path, but SMS frequently never shows because: (a) it arrives only as transient ephemerals and is never fetched from history; (b) the popup list is fed from `/v2/pushes`, which never contains SMS; (c) received SMS is overwritten in the cache by the next display refresh; (d) encrypted SMS is dropped silently.

## Evidence
- No `/v2/permanents/*_threads` fetch anywhere — SMS history is never retrieved. The API client only hits `/v2/pushes`, `/v2/devices`, `/v2/users/me`, `/v2/chats`, `/v2/upload-request` (`src/app/api/client.ts`).
- Popup list source: `fetchDisplayPushes` -> `fetchRecentPushes` (`src/app/api/client.ts:250-308,435-461`); popup renders from `sessionCache.recentPushes` (`src/popup/index.ts:588-625,644-664`).
- `recentPushes` overwrite: `src/app/session/index.ts:143,483`; real-time unshift+save: `src/background/index.ts:491-494`.
- Encrypted drop: `src/background/index.ts:382-438` (early `return` at 437).
- Empty `sms_changed` guard with no fallback: `src/background/utils.ts:409-416`.

## Coupling with Phase A
Because SMS is delivered only as non-replayed ephemerals, a dead socket (Phase A) is itself a leading cause of missing SMS. Phase A must be fixed for Phase B to hold in the real world.

## Children
- B1 preserve received ephemerals (stop overwriting recentPushes).
- B2 surface encrypted SMS.
- B3 fetch SMS thread history via /v2/permanents (the substantive feature).
- B4 diagnostics (depends on B1, B3).

## Success criteria
Received SMS persists in the popup across refresh and SW restart; encrypted SMS yields an actionable prompt; `sms_changed` signals resolve to message content; logs show received/shown/dropped counts by reason.

title: File: split initialized state from WebSocket-connected READY state
description:
## File Scope
Primary file: `src/background/state-machine.ts`

Related files:
- `src/background/index.ts`
- `src/app/session/index.ts`

## Problem
`READY` is documented as authenticated and WebSocket connected, but the code enters `READY` immediately after session initialization. The socket is only started on entry to `READY`.

## Evidence
```ts
// src/background/state-machine.ts
case ServiceWorkerState.INITIALIZING:
  if (event === 'INIT_SUCCESS') {
    return ServiceWorkerState.READY;
  }
```

```ts
// src/background/state-machine.ts
case ServiceWorkerState.READY:
  updateConnectionIcon("connected");

  if (previousState === ServiceWorkerState.INITIALIZING && this.callbacks.onConnectWebSocket) {
    this.callbacks.onConnectWebSocket();
  }
  break;
```

## Mitigation
Add an intermediate state or delay connected UI until `WS_CONNECTED`.

```ts
INITIALIZING + INIT_SUCCESS -> CONNECTING
CONNECTING + WS_CONNECTED -> READY
CONNECTING + WS_DISCONNECTED -> DEGRADED
READY + WS_DISCONNECTED -> DEGRADED
```

If the enum change is too large, preserve the enum but make `READY` promotion happen only after `websocket:connected`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `INIT_SUCCESS` alone does not set connected icon.
- `WS_CONNECTED` proves `READY`.
- Startup and reconnect tests cover the new flow.
acceptance_criteria: READY is reached only when the WebSocket has opened, or a distinct CONNECTING/session-ready state represents initialized-but-not-connected; tests cover INIT_SUCCESS without WS_CONNECTED.

title: Files: honor notification timeout settings for received pushes
description:
## File Scope
Primary files:
- `src/background/utils.ts`
- `src/app/notifications/index.ts`
- `src/background/state.ts`
- `src/options/index.ts`

## Problem
The options page and background state support `notificationTimeout`, but received push notifications are created directly and do not use the timeout helper.

## Evidence
```ts
// src/app/session/index.ts
const notificationTimeoutValue = await storageRepository.getNotificationTimeout();
stateSetters.setNotificationTimeout(notificationTimeoutValue);
```

```ts
// src/background/utils.ts
await chrome.notifications.create(notificationId, finalNotificationOptions);
```

## Mitigation
Use one wrapper for all notification types:

```ts
createNotificationWithTimeout(
  notificationId,
  finalNotificationOptions,
  undefined,
  getNotificationTimeout(),
);
```

If received pushes should persist until dismissal, rename the setting so it does not claim to control them.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Received push notifications honor configured timeout.
- Timeout `0` behavior is documented and tested.
- Link-sent and note-sent notifications keep existing behavior.
- No path duplicates timeout scheduling logic.

title: A5: Keepalive interval correctness (>=30s)
description:
# A5 - Keepalive interval correctness (>= 30s)

Primary file: `src/background/keepalive.ts`

## Problem
`KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 20` -> `periodInMinutes: 20/60 ~= 0.33`. Chrome clamps alarm periods below 0.5 min (30s) in production, so the keepalive does not fire as intended and the inline comment is misleading. Keepalive is also only active during critical operations (reference-counted), not continuously — document this so it is not mistaken for a general service-worker liveness mechanism.

## Evidence
- `src/background/keepalive.ts:7` (`20`), `:20-23` (create with delay/period = 20/60).

## Fix
```ts
const KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 30; // Chrome's minimum alarm period is 30s; lower values are clamped
// ...
chrome.alarms.create(KEEPALIVE_ALARM, {
  delayInMinutes: KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_SECONDS / 60,
  periodInMinutes: KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_SECONDS / 60,
});
```
Add a comment clarifying that keepalive only spans `startCriticalKeepalive()` / `stopCriticalKeepalive()` windows and is not a continuous liveness keeper.

## Acceptance criteria
- Alarm period is >= 0.5 min; behavior during init is unchanged; comment corrected.

## Verification
`npm run typecheck`; existing keepalive/init tests still pass.

## Scope / parallelization
Minor and fully independent.
acceptance_criteria: Alarm period >= 0.5 min; init behavior unchanged; comment corrected.
